summary: Ingress sidecar backpressure amplification causing sustained server-error spike and runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-12 09:30 UTC Acme Retail observed a sustained spike in 500-class responses on their streaming and short-poll routes. Traffic showed elevated error-rate (~18% 5xx) and increased end-to-end latency. Support engagement requested immediate mitigation and root-cause investigation.

Impact: Multi-tenant dedicated cluster serving Acme Retail experienced degraded availability for conversational and embedding endpoints resulting in customer-reported client errors and retry amplification. Critical flows for order chatbots and embedding lookups affected.

Environment: prod-us-east, Dedicated pool (tenant: acme-retail-01), API gateway fronted by ingress-sidecar proxies deployed as a daemonset on edge nodes.

Observed at: 2026-03-12 09:28 UTC first alert from customer dashboard (high 5xx and latency).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues a mix of short chat requests and streaming sessions to the tenant endpoint under sustained high healthcheck/backchannel load
2) In parallel the ingress-sidecar receives a spike of internal healthcheck/backchannel polling (from an internal monitoring job),
3) Connections saturate accept queue and HTTP/2 stream slots; gateway begins returning 502/503/504 while runtimes trigger watchdog restarts
4) Client retries amplify load, maintaining high error rate until throttles are applied
logs: 2026-03-12T09:31:02Z api-gateway: upstream 10.0.5.23:503 timeout reading response; returning 502 to client
2026-03-12T09:32:10Z serving-runtime[worker-7]: watchdog: cpu_spike_detected, threadpool starved, restarting runtime (pid=8421)
2026-03-12T09:33:45Z autoscaler: ephemeral-pool-shed trigger for tenant acme-retail-01 due to backpressure_missmatch
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: kvcache thrashing or GPU OOMs. Verified: no OOMs on host; NVML logs clean.
Detailed traces show majority of 5xx were proxy-layer (502/503) with upstream runtime restarts following proxy accept-queue saturation.
Ingress-sidecar metrics: connection_accept_rate jumped x6, keepalive churn increased, pending-accepts queue grew to 95th percentile of configured max leading to early connection drops.
TLS renegotiation attempts from healthcheck client detected — increased CPU load on proxy and caused HTTP/2 window stalls.
Runtime threadpool starvation correlated with heavy TLS processing on sidecar leading to delayed runtime wakeups and watchdog restarts.

Customer traffic pattern: long-poll streaming + frequent healthcheck/backchannel from internal monitoring job that uses short-lived connections. These combined to create head-of-line blocking on edge accept queues.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:40 - Asha Mehta (Support): Acknowledge ticket and opened investigation. Asked customer to provide client-side timestamps and a pcap of failing sessions.

2026-03-12 09:55 - Diego Morales (SRE): Observed accept-queue saturation on three edge nodes. Spinning up temporary extra proxies to relieve load. Linking logs: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/edge/accept-queue?range=1h
2026-03-12 10:05 - Acme Support Contact (Jordan Lee): Provided client traces and confirmed healthcheck job ran at 09:29 with aggressive parallelism (50 threads).

2026-03-12 10:20 - Diego Morales (SRE): Applied emergency mitigation: rate-limit healthcheck path via ingress-sidecar config and increased accept_queue size on edge nodes. Observed 5xx drop from 18% -> 3% within 6 minutes.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Product Owner (Sofia Nguyen): Requested follow-up action items: durable fix for backpressure, documentation of recommended monitoring knobs for tenants.
2026-03-13 08:12 - Diego Morales (SRE): Running filtering rollout to prevent short-lived TLS renegotiations from monopolizing proxy worker threads. Monitoring for regressions.
resolution:
Mitigation: Applied ingress-sidecar healthcheck rate-limit (temporary ACL) and increased accept_queue on affected edge nodes; rolled back a recent aggressive keepalive-prune config. Result: error-rate reduced to baseline and runtimes stablized.
Long-term: Engineering will implement a sidecar-level backpressure window, add prioritized control plane healthchecks, and harden watchdog thresholds to avoid cascading restarts. Scheduled follow-up: INT-3782 (sidecar backpressure redesign).
